title: A new nested mapping that replaces a scalar uses the step of the mapping it is set in, not the step of an earlier mapping
notes: The document has two nested block mappings with different steps: `x` indents its entry four spaces under its key, and `z`, the mapping that holds `w`, indents its entry two. The patch replaces `/z/w` (the scalar 1) with the mapping `{q: 1}`; there is no sibling mapping to copy. The specification allows any indentation of a nested block mapping greater than its key's, so the bytes rest on a kit convention (docs/edit-semantics.md): the step is taken from the mapping the replaced key belongs to, here two spaces, so `w` is at column 2 and `q` at column 4. A step of four, taken from the earlier mapping, would put `q` at column 6 and fails the case. The case carries the tag `convention`. The result reads back as `x` with `y` 1, and `z` with `w` a mapping of `q` 1. It is the mapping half of the rule that `edit/add-sequence-value-uses-the-enclosing-mappings-step` pins for sequences.
